result.note: Skipped the Jio IPO deal details. Tested SEBI's revised minimum public offer rule and pre-IPO lock-in, plus the 2026 foreign portfolio outflows.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about market rules relating to large initial public offerings (IPOs) in India, as of October 2026:
items: In September 2025, SEBI moved to halve the minimum stake that companies worth over INR 5 trillion must sell, from 5 percent to 2.5 percent.
The finance ministry has written SEBI's change to this minimum stake into the rules.
Under SEBI rules, existing pre-IPO investors cannot sell their stakes for twelve months after the IPO has been allotted.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong because the lock-in for existing investors lasts six months after allotment, not twelve. SEBI said markets may struggle to absorb bigger sales. At Jio's valuation, the old 5 percent minimum would have meant selling about INR 515 billion of stock.
questions.source: In September 2025, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) moved to halve the minimum stake that companies worth over INR 5 trillion (USD 52.5 billion) must sell, from 5 percent to 2.5 percent, saying markets may struggle to absorb bigger sales.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about foreign institutional investor (FII) flows in 2026, as reported in October 2026:
items: FIIs had pulled a record amount from Indian shares during the year, nearly double the total for 2025.
Over the same period, the rupee had fallen nearly 7 percent against the US dollar.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both are correct. FIIs pulled a record INR 3.08 trillion from Indian shares, and the rupee's fall of nearly 7 percent shrank what those investors earn in dollars. Jefferies said domestic mutual funds, fed by monthly savings plans, were absorbing much of the selling.
questions.source: Foreign institutional investors (FII) have pulled a record INR 3.08 trillion (USD 32.4 billion) from Indian shares this year, nearly double 2025’s total.
